segments.text:
The header line. Each later line describes one kernel of bwx12.
- `binary`: the name of the binary. It is `bwx12` in every row.
- `kernel`: the kernel name, as `bwx12 --list` prints it and as the option `--seq` takes it.
- `function`: the C function of the kernel in bwx12.c: `k_` plus the kernel name.
- `start`: the address of the first instruction of the function, in bytes. Hexadecimal, without `0x`.
- `loop_start`: the address of the first instruction of the loop. Hexadecimal. build12.sh takes the target of the first branch that goes backward to an address inside the function [Ref1].
- `loop_mod64`: `loop_start` modulo 64, as a decimal number from 0 to 63. It is the position of the loop start inside a 64-byte block.
segments.heading: Line 1: the six columns

segments.text:
`read` is the new read kernel. Part C runs it.
- The function `k_read` starts at 0x49a0. The loop starts at 0x49a4, 4 bytes (1 instruction) later. That instruction computes the end address of the range.
- 0x49a4 modulo 64 is 36. The loop of `k_read` in bw_new has the same value [Ref3].
- listing.txt shows the loop: 8 `ldp` loads (256 bytes per loop pass), `add`, `cmp` and the backward branch at 0x49cc. That is 11 instructions, 44 bytes [Ref2]. No instruction uses the loaded values.
- The loop starts at position 36 of its 64-byte block and is 44 bytes long. So it ends in the next block: it crosses the boundary at 0x49c0.
segments.heading: Line 2: `read`, the new read kernel

segments.text: No kernel sequence of the whole-chip test names `write` or `copy`. But every thread of a bwx12 process calls `k_write` once before its first interval: it fills its new buffer (the first touch). This call is not timed [Ref4]. Part A times kernels named `write` and `copy`, but they are functions of bw_old and bw_new [Ref8].

`asmread` is the hand-written load-only loop. Part L, part C and control I run it.
- `k_asmread` starts at 0x4ac0. The loop starts at 0x4ad4, 20 bytes (5 instructions) later. Four of them save the registers d8 to d15 on the stack. One computes the end address.
- 0x4ad4 modulo 64 is 20. The loop of `k_asmread` in bw_new has the same value [Ref3].
- The loop has the form of the `read` loop: 8 `ldp` loads (256 bytes per loop pass), `add`, `cmp` and the backward branch (at 0x4afc). That is 11 instructions, 44 bytes [Ref2].
- The loop starts at position 20 and is 44 bytes long. So it lies inside one 64-byte block: the next block starts at 0x4b00, directly after the branch.
segments.heading: Line 5: `asmread`

segments.text: No bwx12 process of the whole-chip test runs these kernels. Part A times kernels named `asmwrite` and `asmcopy`, but they are functions of bw_old and bw_new [Ref8]. The columns have the same meaning.

`oldread` is the old read kernel. Part L, part C and control I run it.
- `k_oldread` starts at 0x4600. The loop starts at 0x4668, 104 bytes (26 instructions) later. These instructions make the stack frame, store the stack guard value, set the 16 sums to zero and compute the number of loop passes.
- 0x4668 modulo 64 is 40. The loop of `k_read` in bw_old has the same value [Ref3].
- listing.txt shows the loop: 4 `ldp` loads (128 bytes per loop pass), 8 vector adds (one per loaded register), 2 scalar `add` (pass counter and address), `cmp` and the backward branch at 0x46a4. That is 16 instructions, 64 bytes [Ref2].
- The loop starts at position 40 and is 64 bytes long. So it crosses the boundary at 0x4680.
segments.heading: Line 8: `oldread`, the old read kernel

segments.text: The whole-chip test does not run these kernels. The columns have the same meaning. `asmread2`, `asmwrite2`, `asmcopy2` and `oldread2` are second copies: the same source under a second name. Each has the `loop_mod64` of its original: 20, 40, 52 and 40.

`read_1pl` is the test loop with one load per 64-byte line. Part L and control I run it.
- `k_read_1pl` starts at 0x55d0. The loop starts at 0x55d4, 4 bytes (1 instruction) later.
- 0x55d4 modulo 64 is 20, the value of `asmread`.
- listing.txt shows the loop: 4 `ldr` loads of 16 bytes each, at the offsets 0, 64, 128 and 192 of a 256-byte block, then `add`, `cmp` and the backward branch at 0x55ec. That is 7 instructions, 28 bytes [Ref2]. So one loop pass loads 64 bytes and moves the address forward by 256 bytes.
- bwx12 counts the length of the range that a kernel call covers, not the loaded bytes. So it counts 256 bytes per loop pass of `read_1pl` [Ref4].
segments.heading: Line 27: `read_1pl`

segments.text: The whole-chip test does not run this kernel.

`read_nop96` is the `asmread` loop with 96 `nop` instructions per loop pass. Part L and control I run it.
- `k_read_nop96` starts at 0x57c0. The loop starts at 0x57d4, 20 bytes later, after the same 5 instructions as in `k_asmread`.
- 0x57d4 modulo 64 is 20, the value of `asmread`.
- listing.txt shows the loop: 8 `ldp` loads (256 bytes per loop pass), 96 `nop`, `add`, `cmp` and the backward branch at 0x597c. That is 107 instructions, 428 bytes [Ref2].
segments.heading: Line 29: `read_nop96`

segments.text: The whole-chip test does not run these kernels. They are the `asmread` loop with other numbers of `nop` instructions. Each loop starts at 20 modulo 64.

`read_nop256` is the `asmread` loop with 256 `nop` instructions per loop pass. Part L and control I run it.
- `k_read_nop256` starts at 0x6cc0. The loop starts at 0x6cd4, 20 bytes later, after the same 5 instructions as in `k_asmread`.
- 0x6cd4 modulo 64 is 20, the value of `asmread`.
- listing.txt shows the loop: 8 `ldp` loads (256 bytes per loop pass), 256 `nop`, `add`, `cmp` and the backward branch at 0x70fc. That is 267 instructions, 1068 bytes [Ref2].
segments.heading: Line 39: `read_nop256`

segments.text: The whole-chip test does not run these kernels. They are read loops with vector adds (`read_dadd`, `read_iadd16`), read loops of 128 bytes per loop pass (`read_sp`), `read_1pl_nop96`, and write and copy loops with `nop` instructions. The read loops start at 20 modulo 64, the write loops at 40 and the copy loops at 52.
